Appendix A Proofs for Spectral Analysis of Denoising Regression

Throughout the appendices the diffusion time t∈(0,T]t\in(0,T] is fixed, 𝔼[⋅∣t]\mathbb{E}[\,\cdot\mid t] denotes the expectation over the pair (𝐱0,𝐱t)(\mathbf{x}_{0},\mathbf{x}_{t}) at time tt, k∈{0,…,n−1}k\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\} indexes the graph frequencies, and qk=σ2/λγ,kq_{k}=\sigma^{2}/\lambda_{\gamma,k} is the prior power at λk\lambda_{k}, so that the power ratio is gk=pk/qkg_{k}=p_{k}/q_{k}. Since c¯t>0\bar{c}_{t}>0 by (11) and λγ,k≥γ>0\lambda_{\gamma,k}\geq\gamma>0 by (9), the attenuation at,ka_{t,k} and the noise variance νt,k\nu_{t,k} satisfy

at,k=e−λγ,k​c¯t∈(0,1),ρt,k≥νt,k=qk​(1−at,k2)>0.a_{t,k}=e^{-\lambda_{\gamma,k}\bar{c}_{t}}\in(0,1),\quad\rho_{t,k}\geq\nu_{t,k}=q_{k}\bigl(1-a_{t,k}^{2}\bigr)>0. (51)

Gradient flow is the continuous-time limit of gradient descent as the step size tends to zero. A trainable vector 𝝃\boldsymbol{\xi} that minimizes an objective 𝒥\mathcal{J} evolves from an initialization 𝝃⁡(0)\boldsymbol{\xi}(0) as

d​𝝃​(τ)d​τ=−η​∇𝝃𝒥​(𝝃⁡(τ)),τ≥0,\frac{d\boldsymbol{\xi}(\tau)}{d\tau}=-\eta\,\nabla_{\boldsymbol{\xi}}\mathcal{J}\bigl(\boldsymbol{\xi}(\tau)\bigr),\qquad\tau\geq 0, (52)

with optimization time τ\tau and learning rate η>0\eta>0. Under a shared diffusion rate, SNRt,k\snr_{t,k} depends on tt only through c¯t\bar{c}_{t}, and we write SNRk⁡(c¯)\snr_{k}(\bar{c}) for this dependence.

To help exposition, each proof is preceded by an auxiliary lemma. The proofs of the lemmas are provided in Appendix D.

Lemma 1 (Optimal linear denoiser).

Let Assumptions 1 and 2 hold, and let t∈(0,T]t\in(0,T]. Then, the unique minimizer of the fixed-time error ℒt​(f𝐖)\mathcal{L}_{t}(f_{\mathbf{W}}) over 𝐖∈ℝn×n\mathbf{W}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n} is the spectral graph filter denoiser (28) with the frequency response (29).

Proof of Proposition 1.

By Lemma 1, the optimal linear denoiser is a spectral graph filter. Restricting the fixed-time error to 𝐖=𝐕​𝖽𝗂𝖺𝗀​(𝐡t)​𝐕𝖳\mathbf{W}=\mathbf{V}\mathsf{diag}(\mathbf{h}_{t})\mathbf{V}^{\mathsf{T}} separates it across graph frequencies,

ℒt​(f𝐡t)=∑k=0n−1ℓt,k​(ht,k),ℓt,k​(h)=𝔼⁡[(x~0,k−h​x~t,k)2∣t],\mathcal{L}_{t}(f_{\mathbf{h}_{t}})=\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\ell_{t,k}(h_{t,k}),\quad\ell_{t,k}(h)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[(\tilde{x}_{0,k}-h\tilde{x}_{t,k})^{2}\mid t\bigr], (53)

with ℓt,k\ell_{t,k} the error at λk\lambda_{k}. The noise e~t,k\tilde{e}_{t,k} is zero-mean and independent of 𝐱0\mathbf{x}_{0}, hence 𝔼⁡[x~0,k​x~t,k∣t]=at,k​pk\mathbb{E}[\tilde{x}_{0,k}\tilde{x}_{t,k}\mid t]=a_{t,k}p_{k}, 𝔼⁡[x~t,k 2∣t]=ρt,k\mathbb{E}[\tilde{x}_{t,k}^{\,2}\mid t]=\rho_{t,k}, and ℓt,k​(h)=pk−2​at,k​pk​h+ρt,k​h2\ell_{t,k}(h)=p_{k}-2a_{t,k}p_{k}\,h+\rho_{t,k}h^{2}. Completing the square in ℓt,k​(h)\ell_{t,k}(h) with ht,k⋆h_{t,k}^{\star} of (29) gives

ℓt,k​(h)=ρt,k​(h−ht,k⋆)2+pk−at,k2​pk2ρt,k.\ell_{t,k}(h)=\rho_{t,k}\bigl(h-h_{t,k}^{\star}\bigr)^{2}+p_{k}-\frac{a_{t,k}^{2}p_{k}^{2}}{\rho_{t,k}}. (54)

Summing over kk gives the fixed-time error of the spectral graph filter as a separable quadratic,

ℒt​(f𝐡t)=ℬt+∑k=0n−1ρt,k​(ht,k−ht,k⋆)2,\mathcal{L}_{t}(f_{\mathbf{h}_{t}})=\mathcal{B}_{t}+\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\rho_{t,k}\bigl(h_{t,k}-h_{t,k}^{\star}\bigr)^{2}, (55)

with constant Hessian 2​𝖽𝗂𝖺𝗀​(ρt,0,…,ρt,n−1)2\mathsf{diag}(\rho_{t,0},\ldots,\rho_{t,n-1}) and with ℬt\mathcal{B}_{t} the sum of the constant terms in (54). At h=ht,k⋆h=h_{t,k}^{\star} only the constant term remains. Since ρt,k−at,k2​pk=νt,k\rho_{t,k}-a_{t,k}^{2}p_{k}=\nu_{t,k} by (27) and ρt,k/νt,k=1+SNRt,k\rho_{t,k}/\nu_{t,k}=1+\snr_{t,k} by Definition 2,

ℓt,k​(ht,k⋆)=pk​νt,kρt,k=pk1+SNRt,k.\ell_{t,k}(h_{t,k}^{\star})=\frac{p_{k}\nu_{t,k}}{\rho_{t,k}}=\frac{p_{k}}{1+\snr_{t,k}}. (56)

Dividing (56) by pk>0p_{k}>0 gives (30). Summing (56) over kk gives (31), and Lemma 1 makes this sum the minimum over the whole linear class. ∎

Proof of Proposition 2.

By (55), ∂ℒt​(f𝐡t)/∂ht,k=2​ρt,k​(ht,k−ht,k⋆)\partial\mathcal{L}_{t}(f_{\mathbf{h}_{t}})/\partial h_{t,k}=2\rho_{t,k}(h_{t,k}-h_{t,k}^{\star}) depends on ht,kh_{t,k} alone. The gradient flow (52) with 𝝃=𝐡t\boldsymbol{\xi}=\mathbf{h}_{t} therefore splits into the nn scalar equations

d​ht,k​(τ)d​τ=−2ηρt,k(ht,k(τ)−ht,k⋆),k=0,…,n−1.\frac{dh_{t,k}(\tau)}{d\tau}=-2\eta\,\rho_{t,k}\bigl(h_{t,k}(\tau)-h_{t,k}^{\star}\bigr),\quad k=0,\ldots,n-1. (57)

Fix a graph frequency λk\lambda_{k} and set hˇt,k​(τ)=ht,k​(τ)−ht,k⋆\check{h}_{t,k}(\tau)=h_{t,k}(\tau)-h_{t,k}^{\star}, where the optimal frequency response ht,k⋆h_{t,k}^{\star} does not depend on τ\tau. Then

dd​τ​[e2​η​ρt,k​τ​hˇt,k​(τ)]=e2​η​ρt,k​τ​[d​hˇt,kd​τ+2​η​ρt,k​hˇt,k]=0,\frac{d}{d\tau}\Bigl[e^{2\eta\rho_{t,k}\tau}\check{h}_{t,k}(\tau)\Bigr]=e^{2\eta\rho_{t,k}\tau}\Bigl[\frac{d\check{h}_{t,k}}{d\tau}+2\eta\rho_{t,k}\check{h}_{t,k}\Bigr]=0, (58)

hence hˇt,k​(τ)=e−2​η​ρt,k​τ​hˇt,k​(0)\check{h}_{t,k}(\tau)=e^{-2\eta\rho_{t,k}\tau}\check{h}_{t,k}(0), which is (32) with τt,k=(2​η​ρt,k)−1\tau_{t,k}=(2\eta\rho_{t,k})^{-1}. ∎

Lemma 2 (Informative window).

Let the diffusion rate be shared, and let pk>0p_{k}>0. Then, the set of integrated-rate values at which graph frequency λk\lambda_{k} is ε\varepsilon-informative,

ℐk​(ε)={c¯≥0:ε≤SNRk⁡(c¯)≤ε−1},\mathcal{I}_{k}(\varepsilon)=\bigl\{\bar{c}\geq 0\;:\;\varepsilon\leq\snr_{k}(\bar{c})\leq\varepsilon^{-1}\bigr\}, (59)

is the interval

ℐk​(ε)=[log⁡(1+gk​ε)2​λγ,k,log⁡(1+gk​ε−1)2​λγ,k],\mathcal{I}_{k}(\varepsilon)=\left[\frac{\log(1+g_{k}\varepsilon)}{2\lambda_{\gamma,k}},\;\frac{\log(1+g_{k}\varepsilon^{-1})}{2\lambda_{\gamma,k}}\right], (60)

and its length satisfies

|ℐk​(ε)|=12​λγ,k​log⁡1+gk​ε−11+gk​ε≤log⁡(1/ε)λγ,k.\bigl|\mathcal{I}_{k}(\varepsilon)\bigr|=\frac{1}{2\lambda_{\gamma,k}}\log\frac{1+g_{k}\varepsilon^{-1}}{1+g_{k}\varepsilon}\;\leq\;\frac{\log(1/\varepsilon)}{\lambda_{\gamma,k}}. (61)
Proof of Proposition 3.

Evaluating (60) at c¯=c¯t>0\bar{c}=\bar{c}_{t}>0, graph frequency λk\lambda_{k} is informative at time tt if and only if

log⁡(1+gk​ε)2​c¯t≤λγ,k≤log⁡(1+gk​ε−1)2​c¯t.\frac{\log(1+g_{k}\varepsilon)}{2\bar{c}_{t}}\;\leq\;\lambda_{\gamma,k}\;\leq\;\frac{\log(1+g_{k}\varepsilon^{-1})}{2\bar{c}_{t}}. (62)

Let jj and kk both be informative at time tt. Take the upper bound in (62) for jj and the lower bound for kk. Since log⁡(1+x)\log(1+x) increases, gj≤gmaxg_{j}\leq g_{\max} and gk≥gmin>0g_{k}\geq g_{\min}>0,

λγ,jλγ,k≤log⁡(1+gj​ε−1)log⁡(1+gk​ε)≤log⁡(1+gmax​ε−1)log⁡(1+gmin​ε).∎\frac{\lambda_{\gamma,j}}{\lambda_{\gamma,k}}\leq\frac{\log(1+g_{j}\varepsilon^{-1})}{\log(1+g_{k}\varepsilon)}\leq\frac{\log\bigl(1+g_{\max}\varepsilon^{-1}\bigr)}{\log\bigl(1+g_{\min}\varepsilon\bigr)}.\qed
Lemma 3 (Orthogonality of the posterior mean).

Let t∈(0,T]t\in(0,T]. Then, for every random variable zz that is a function of 𝐱t\mathbf{x}_{t},

𝔼[(x~0,k−mt,k)z|t]=0,k=0,…,n−1.\mathbb{E}\bigl[(\tilde{x}_{0,k}-m_{t,k})\,z\,\big|\,t\bigr]=0,\qquad k=0,\ldots,n-1. (63)

Let mt,k=[𝐕𝖳​𝗆t​(𝐱t)]km_{t,k}=[\mathbf{V}^{\mathsf{T}}\mathsf{m}_{t}(\mathbf{x}_{t})]_{k} and x~^0,k=[𝐕𝖳​fΘ​(𝐱t,𝐋,t)]k\widehat{\tilde{x}}_{0,k}=[\mathbf{V}^{\mathsf{T}}f_{\Theta}(\mathbf{x}_{t},\mathbf{L},t)]_{k} be the kkth GFT coefficients of the posterior mean and of the GNN output, as in Proposition 4. At graph frequency λk\lambda_{k}, we denote the MMSE, the gain of the posterior mean over the optimal linear denoiser, and the error of the GNN with respect to the posterior mean by

MMSEt,k\displaystyle\mmse_{t,k} =𝔼⁡[(x~0,k−mt,k)2|t],\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}\!\left[(\tilde{x}_{0,k}-m_{t,k})^{2}\,\middle|\,t\right], (64)
Δt,k\displaystyle\Delta_{t,k} =𝔼⁡[(mt,k−ht,k⋆​x~t,k)2|t],\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}\!\left[(m_{t,k}-h_{t,k}^{\star}\tilde{x}_{t,k})^{2}\,\middle|\,t\right],
ωt,k\displaystyle\omega_{t,k} =𝔼⁡[(mt,k−x~^0,k)2|t],\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}\!\left[(m_{t,k}-\widehat{\tilde{x}}_{0,k})^{2}\,\middle|\,t\right],

with sums MMSEt=∑kMMSEt,k\mmse_{t}=\sum_{k}\mmse_{t,k}, ΔPM,t=∑kΔt,k\Delta_{\mathrm{PM},t}=\sum_{k}\Delta_{t,k} and ΩΘ,t=∑kωt,k\Omega_{\Theta,t}=\sum_{k}\omega_{t,k}. The three estimates ht,k⋆​x~t,kh_{t,k}^{\star}\tilde{x}_{t,k}, mt,km_{t,k} and x~^0,k\widehat{\tilde{x}}_{0,k} are functions of 𝐱t\mathbf{x}_{t}, and Lemma 3 splits the error of each one around the posterior mean. First, write x~0,k−x~^0,k=(x~0,k−mt,k)+(mt,k−x~^0,k)\tilde{x}_{0,k}-\widehat{\tilde{x}}_{0,k}=(\tilde{x}_{0,k}-m_{t,k})+(m_{t,k}-\widehat{\tilde{x}}_{0,k}) and take the second moment. The cross term vanishes by (63) with z=mt,k−x~^0,kz=m_{t,k}-\widehat{\tilde{x}}_{0,k}, and the two remaining terms are MMSEt,k\mmse_{t,k} and ωt,k\omega_{t,k}. Second, write x~0,k−ht,k⋆​x~t,k=(x~0,k−mt,k)+(mt,k−ht,k⋆​x~t,k)\tilde{x}_{0,k}-h_{t,k}^{\star}\tilde{x}_{t,k}=(\tilde{x}_{0,k}-m_{t,k})+(m_{t,k}-h_{t,k}^{\star}\tilde{x}_{t,k}). The cross term vanishes with z=mt,k−ht,k⋆​x~t,kz=m_{t,k}-h_{t,k}^{\star}\tilde{x}_{t,k}, and the second moment of the left side is pk​dt,kp_{k}d_{t,k} by (30). Third, write x~0,k=(x~0,k−mt,k)+mt,k\tilde{x}_{0,k}=(\tilde{x}_{0,k}-m_{t,k})+m_{t,k} and take z=mt,kz=m_{t,k}. The three identities are

𝔼⁡[(x~0,k−x~^0,k)2∣t]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\bigl[(\tilde{x}_{0,k}-\widehat{\tilde{x}}_{0,k})^{2}\mid t\bigr] =MMSEt,k+ωt,k,\displaystyle=\mmse_{t,k}+\omega_{t,k}, (65)
pk​dt,k\displaystyle p_{k}\,d_{t,k} =MMSEt,k+Δt,k,\displaystyle=\mmse_{t,k}+\Delta_{t,k},
pk\displaystyle p_{k} =MMSEt,k+𝔼⁡[mt,k2∣t].\displaystyle=\mmse_{t,k}+\mathbb{E}\bigl[m_{t,k}^{2}\mid t\bigr].
Proof of Proposition 4.

Since 𝐕\mathbf{V} is orthogonal, every 𝐳∈ℝn\mathbf{z}\in\mathbb{R}^{n} satisfies ‖𝐳‖22=∑k[𝐕𝖳​𝐳]k2\|\mathbf{z}\|_{2}^{2}=\sum_{k}[\mathbf{V}^{\mathsf{T}}\mathbf{z}]_{k}^{2}. Summing the first line of (65) over kk therefore gives

ℒt​(fΘ)=MMSEt+ΩΘ,t.\mathcal{L}_{t}(f_{\Theta})=\mmse_{t}+\Omega_{\Theta,t}. (66)

Summing the second line over kk, with ℬt=∑kpk​dt,k\mathcal{B}_{t}=\sum_{k}p_{k}d_{t,k} from (31), gives

MMSEt=ℬt−ΔPM,t.\mmse_{t}=\mathcal{B}_{t}-\Delta_{\mathrm{PM},t}. (67)

Substituting (67) into (66) yields (34). Both ΔPM,t\Delta_{\mathrm{PM},t} and ΩΘ,t\Omega_{\Theta,t} are sums of expected squares and hence nonnegative. ∎

Proof of Corollary 1.

Eliminating MMSEt,k\mmse_{t,k} between the last two lines of (65) and using 1−dt,k=SNRt,k/(1+SNRt,k)1-d_{t,k}=\snr_{t,k}/(1+\snr_{t,k}) from (30),

𝔼⁡[mt,k2∣t]=pk​(1−dt,k)+Δt,k=pk​SNRt,k1+SNRt,k+Δt,k.∎\mathbb{E}\bigl[m_{t,k}^{2}\mid t\bigr]=p_{k}\bigl(1-d_{t,k}\bigr)+\Delta_{t,k}=p_{k}\frac{\snr_{t,k}}{1+\snr_{t,k}}+\Delta_{t,k}.\qed

Appendix B Tangent-Kernel Dynamics of the GNN Denoiser

Let PP be the number of parameters of fΘf_{\Theta}. Under the gradient flow (52), the GNN moves through the Jacobian of its output with respect to the parameters and through the tangent kernel,

𝐉Θ​(𝐱,t)=∇ΘfΘ​(𝐱,𝐋,t)∈ℝn×P,𝐊Θ,t​(𝐱,𝐱′)=𝐉Θ​(𝐱,t)​𝐉Θ​(𝐱′,t)𝖳∈ℝn×n.\begin{gathered}\mathbf{J}_{\Theta}(\mathbf{x},t)=\nabla_{\Theta}f_{\Theta}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{L},t)\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times P},\\ \mathbf{K}_{\Theta,t}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{x}^{\prime})=\mathbf{J}_{\Theta}(\mathbf{x},t)\,\mathbf{J}_{\Theta}(\mathbf{x}^{\prime},t)^{\mathsf{T}}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}.\end{gathered} (68)

The kernel records how far a gradient step taken at 𝐱′\mathbf{x}^{\prime} moves the output at 𝐱\mathbf{x}. Recall that πt\pi_{t} is the law of the corrupted signal 𝐱t\mathbf{x}_{t}, and let 𝐫τ=fΘ⁡(τ)​(⋅,𝐋,t)−𝗆t\mathbf{r}_{\tau}=f_{\Theta(\tau)}(\cdot,\mathbf{L},t)-\mathsf{m}_{t} be the residual with respect to the posterior mean at optimization time τ\tau. Its squared norm under πt\pi_{t} is the excess error ΩΘ⁡(τ),t\Omega_{\Theta(\tau),t} in (34). We write 𝐉τ​(𝐱)=𝐉Θ⁡(τ)​(𝐱,t)\mathbf{J}_{\tau}(\mathbf{x})=\mathbf{J}_{\Theta(\tau)}(\mathbf{x},t), 𝐊τ=𝐊Θ⁡(τ),t\mathbf{K}_{\tau}=\mathbf{K}_{\Theta(\tau),t} and 𝔼′​[⋅]=𝔼𝐱′∼πt​[⋅]\mathbb{E}^{\prime}[\,\cdot\,]=\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{x}^{\prime}\sim\pi_{t}}[\,\cdot\,]. Differentiating ℒt​(fΘ)\mathcal{L}_{t}(f_{\Theta}) under the expectation and conditioning on 𝐱t=𝐱′\mathbf{x}_{t}=\mathbf{x}^{\prime}, with 𝔼[𝐱0∣𝐱t=𝐱′,t]=𝗆t(𝐱′)\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{x}_{0}\mid\mathbf{x}_{t}=\mathbf{x}^{\prime},t]=\mathsf{m}_{t}(\mathbf{x}^{\prime}), gives

∇Θℒt​(fΘ)\displaystyle\nabla_{\Theta}\mathcal{L}_{t}(f_{\Theta}) =−2​𝔼​[𝐉τ​(𝐱t)𝖳​(𝐱0−fΘ⁡(τ)​(𝐱t,𝐋,t))|t]\displaystyle=-2\,\mathbb{E}\bigl[\mathbf{J}_{\tau}(\mathbf{x}_{t})^{\mathsf{T}}\bigl(\mathbf{x}_{0}-f_{\Theta(\tau)}(\mathbf{x}_{t},\mathbf{L},t)\bigr)\,\big|\,t\bigr] (69)
=2​𝔼′​[𝐉τ​(𝐱′)𝖳​𝐫τ​(𝐱′)].\displaystyle=2\,\mathbb{E}^{\prime}\bigl[\mathbf{J}_{\tau}(\mathbf{x}^{\prime})^{\mathsf{T}}\mathbf{r}_{\tau}(\mathbf{x}^{\prime})\bigr].

The posterior mean 𝗆t\mathsf{m}_{t} does not depend on τ\tau. The chain rule with (52) and (68) gives the residual flow

∂𝐫τ​(𝐱)∂τ=−η​𝐉τ​(𝐱)​∇Θℒt​(fΘ)=−2​η​𝔼′​[𝐊τ​(𝐱,𝐱′)​𝐫τ​(𝐱′)].\frac{\partial\mathbf{r}_{\tau}(\mathbf{x})}{\partial\tau}=-\eta\,\mathbf{J}_{\tau}(\mathbf{x})\nabla_{\Theta}\mathcal{L}_{t}(f_{\Theta})=-2\eta\,\mathbb{E}^{\prime}\bigl[\mathbf{K}_{\tau}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{x}^{\prime})\mathbf{r}_{\tau}(\mathbf{x}^{\prime})\bigr]. (70)

Resolving the residual and the kernel in the graph Fourier basis, r~τ,k​(𝐱)=[𝐕𝖳​𝐫τ​(𝐱)]k\tilde{r}_{\tau,k}(\mathbf{x})=[\mathbf{V}^{\mathsf{T}}\mathbf{r}_{\tau}(\mathbf{x})]_{k} and K~τ,j​k​(𝐱,𝐱′)=𝐯j𝖳​𝐊τ​(𝐱,𝐱′)​𝐯k\tilde{K}_{\tau,jk}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{x}^{\prime})=\mathbf{v}_{j}^{\mathsf{T}}\mathbf{K}_{\tau}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{x}^{\prime})\mathbf{v}_{k}, and inserting 𝐕𝐕𝖳=𝐈\mathbf{V}\mathbf{V}^{\mathsf{T}}=\mathbf{I} before 𝐫τ​(𝐱′)\mathbf{r}_{\tau}(\mathbf{x}^{\prime}) in (70) gives the frequency-wise form

∂r~τ,j​(𝐱)∂τ=−2η∑k=0n−1𝔼′[K~τ,j​k(𝐱,𝐱′)r~τ,k(𝐱′)].\frac{\partial\tilde{r}_{\tau,j}(\mathbf{x})}{\partial\tau}=-2\eta\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\mathbb{E}^{\prime}\bigl[\tilde{K}_{\tau,jk}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{x}^{\prime})\,\tilde{r}_{\tau,k}(\mathbf{x}^{\prime})\bigr]. (71)

The off-diagonal entries K~τ,j​k\tilde{K}_{\tau,jk} with j≠kj\neq k are what couples the graph frequencies. For the spectral graph filter (28) with Θ=𝐡t\Theta=\mathbf{h}_{t}, the kernel in the graph Fourier basis is 𝐕𝖳​𝐊τ​(𝐱,𝐱′)​𝐕=𝖽𝗂𝖺𝗀⁡(𝐱~)​𝖽𝗂𝖺𝗀​(𝐱~′)\mathbf{V}^{\mathsf{T}}\mathbf{K}_{\tau}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{x}^{\prime})\mathbf{V}=\mathsf{diag}(\mathbf{\tilde{x}})\mathsf{diag}(\mathbf{\tilde{x}}^{\prime}). It is diagonal, so (71) reduces to (57). The linear operations in (5) act separately across graph Fourier modes, but shared parameters can still couple modes in the tangent kernel. For example, the linear model fθ​(𝐱)=θ​𝐱f_{\theta}(\mathbf{x})=\theta\mathbf{x} has K~τ,j​k​(𝐱,𝐱′)=x~j​x~k′\tilde{K}_{\tau,jk}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{x}^{\prime})=\tilde{x}_{j}\tilde{x}^{\prime}_{k}, which is generally nonzero for j≠kj\neq k.

For the GNN the kernel moves with Θ⁡(τ)\Theta(\tau), and (70) is nonlinear in the residual. Freezing the kernel at 𝐊t\mathbf{K}_{t} is the standard tangent-kernel linearization [89, 90, 91], which we use only to identify which quantities depend on the diffusion rate. Under this linearization, the flow is generated by the linear integral operator

(𝒯t​𝗎)​(𝐱)=𝔼′​[𝐊t​(𝐱,𝐱′)​𝗎​(𝐱′)],𝗎∈L2​(πt,ℝn),\bigl(\mathcal{T}_{t}\mathsf{u}\bigr)(\mathbf{x})=\mathbb{E}^{\prime}\bigl[\mathbf{K}_{t}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{x}^{\prime})\,\mathsf{u}(\mathbf{x}^{\prime})\bigr],\quad\mathsf{u}\in L^{2}(\pi_{t};\mathbb{R}^{n}), (72)

which plays the role of the Hessian in (55). The flow becomes linear and solvable,

∂𝐫τ∂τ=−2​η​𝒯t​𝐫τ,𝐫τ=e−2​η​𝒯t​τ​𝐫0,\frac{\partial\mathbf{r}_{\tau}}{\partial\tau}=-2\eta\,\mathcal{T}_{t}\mathbf{r}_{\tau},\qquad\mathbf{r}_{\tau}=e^{-2\eta\mathcal{T}_{t}\tau}\mathbf{r}_{0}, (73)

whose exponential rates are given by the eigenvalues of 𝒯t\mathcal{T}_{t}. For a fixed kernel function and initialization, the flow (73) depends on the diffusion rate only through the law πt\pi_{t} and the posterior mean 𝗆t\mathsf{m}_{t}, which at a fixed time are determined by the data law, at,ka_{t,k} and νt,k\nu_{t,k}.

To conclude this appendix, we provide the proposition that shows the bound in (46).

Proposition 5 (Stiffness under a shared diffusion rate).

Let Assumption 2 hold, let the diffusion rate ctc_{t} be shared and nondecreasing, and let the horizon be δ\delta-complete with SNRT,n−1≤1/3\snr_{T,n-1}\leq 1/3. Then, for the optimal linear denoiser (29), the reverse-time stiffness (46) satisfies

LSshared≥log⁡(1/δ)4​T​cond⁡(𝐋γ).L_{S}^{\mathrm{shared}}\geq\frac{\log(1/\delta)}{4T}\,\cond(\mathbf{L}_{\gamma}). (78)
Proof of Proposition 5.

At the highest graph frequency, the assumption gives SNRT,n−1≤1/3\snr_{T,n-1}\leq 1/3. By (29), 2​aT,n−1​hT,n−1⋆=2​SNRT,n−1/(1+SNRT,n−1)2a_{T,n-1}h_{T,n-1}^{\star}=2\snr_{T,n-1}/(1+\snr_{T,n-1}), which increases with the SNR and is therefore at most 12\tfrac{1}{2}. The numerator of the local stiffness ζT,n−1\zeta_{T,n-1} at time TT is then at least 12\tfrac{1}{2}, and its denominator 1−aT,n−121-a_{T,n-1}^{2} is at most one. Since LSshared=suptmaxk⁡|ζt,k|L_{S}^{\mathrm{shared}}=\sup_{t}\max_{k}|\zeta_{t,k}| for a spectral graph filter,

LSshared≥|ζT,n−1|≥12​cT​λγ,max.L_{S}^{\mathrm{shared}}\geq|\zeta_{T,n-1}|\geq\frac{1}{2}\,c_{T}\lambda_{\gamma,\max}. (79)

It remains to bound the terminal diffusion rate cTc_{T}. A nondecreasing diffusion rate gives c¯T=∫0Tcs​𝑑s≤T​cT\bar{c}_{T}=\int_{0}^{T}c_{s}\,ds\leq Tc_{T}, and δ\delta-completeness gives c¯T≥log⁡(1/δ)/(2​γ)\bar{c}_{T}\geq\log(1/\delta)/(2\gamma). Hence cT≥log⁡(1/δ)/(2​γ​T)c_{T}\geq\log(1/\delta)/(2\gamma T). Substituting this bound into (79) and using λγ,max/γ=cond⁡(𝐋γ)\lambda_{\gamma,\max}/\gamma=\cond(\mathbf{L}_{\gamma}) gives (78). ∎

Both matrices are diagonal in 𝐕\mathbf{V}. The kkth diagonal entry of 𝐌t\mathbf{M}_{t} is at,k​pka_{t,k}p_{k} and that of 𝐑t\mathbf{R}_{t} is the corrupted power ρt,k\rho_{t,k}. The fixed-time error of a linear denoiser expands as [92]
